key_points: Cross-session credential leakage: another user's production server credentials (IP, root username, plaintext password) appeared in a different user's Claude Code session
Two-way breach: inbound leak (another user's secrets in my context) and outbound action (unauthorized SSH + database migration on third-party production DB)
Credentials for host 8.211.46.34 surfaced in a session belonging to a user who only owns 59.110.139.37
Real database modifications (INSERTs/UPDATEs) executed against tk_dist PostgreSQL database (pricing/subscription tables)
Breaks core tenant-isolation guarantee of Claude Code
VSCode extension captures IDE selection from closed, never-saved files and transmits to model context
Selected text containing a live Google OAuth client secret (GOCSPX-...) was leaked
Closing the editor and never persisting the file did not prevent selection from being read and sent to the model
Selection/context capture outlives the editor lifecycle and ignores unsaved/closed state
Vanilla Claude Code reads credential files (rclone.conf, secrets.yaml, .credentials, private keys) straight into the transcript and API
Real incidents: Google Drive OAuth tokens leaked, RTSP URLs with embedded credentials echoed, backup encryption passwords exposed
Users forced to build custom PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks for path-based guards, shape guards, output scanners, and OCR guards
Argues this should be native, default-on protection, not requiring five custom hooks per machine
Critical command injection vulnerabilities discovered in Claude Code
Advisory published April 16, 2026
Recommendations: update immediately, stop using authentication helpers, set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY directly
Review .claude/settings.json changes in PRs as carefully as code changes
Never run CLI against untrusted pull requests in CI/CD pipelines
Coding agents in GitHub Actions pose hidden security risks
AI coding agents running in CI/CD pipelines can be exploited via malicious PRs
Settings files (.claude/settings.json) can be weaponized for command injection
Need for sandbox isolation and least-privilege principles for AI agents

stats.fact: Claude Code cross-session credential leakage issue (#72274) reported June 29, 2026 — another user's production server credentials appeared in a different user's session, leading to unauthorized database modifications
VSCode extension selection leak (#71566): closed, never-saved file contents with secrets (Google OAuth client secret) transmitted to model context
Alibaba banned Claude Code from workplace over alleged backdoor risks (July 3, 2026)
Anthropic announced Project Glasswing (April 7, 2026) — Claude Mythos Preview found thousands of high-severity vulnerabilities in every major OS and web browser
Critical command injection vulnerabilities in Claude Code disclosed April 16, 2026 — users advised to update immediately and avoid authentication helpers
Claude Code has over 70,000+ open GitHub issues, with multiple security-related bugs including credential leakage, context bleed, and safety filter bypasses

angles: The 'two-way breach' problem: Claude Code not only leaks your data to others, but also receives and acts on other people's credentials — making it a vector for both data exfiltration AND unauthorized actions on your infrastructure
The 'closed tab doesn't mean gone' issue: IDE selection capture outlives editor lifecycle, meaning secrets you thought were discarded can still be transmitted
Enterprise compliance nightmare: cross-tenant data leakage breaks fundamental SaaS isolation guarantees, making Claude Code a liability for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and GDPR compliance
The DIY security tax: users are forced to build elaborate custom guard hooks (path guards, shape scanners, output monitors) that should be built-in
Alibaba's ban as a canary in the coal mine: if a major Chinese tech conglomerate bans Claude Code over security concerns, enterprise adoption elsewhere may follow
